newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus government bonds make debut on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus government bonds make debut on bourse.

text.p: Cyprus government bonds worth 21 million pounds ($41.2 million) made their debut on the Cyprus Stock Exchange on Wednesday, bourse officials said.
"Trading started this morning," said Nondas Metaxas, director of the bourse. "Naturally we expect the demand for the bonds to be high," he told Reuters.
The middle market price of the bonds closed at 100.80 pounds. No trading was recorded.
But trading volumes were generally subdued, not fully recovered from the extended break because of the Greek Orthodox Easter celebrated on Sunday and Monday.
Trading volume on the 41-share bourse was 318,271 pounds on Wednesday, compared with an average volume of 619,500 last week.
The bonds, initially auctioned on a competitive and non-competitive basis by the central bank on April 15, have a coupon of seven percent, payable half yearly.
At the central bank auction, the average price of competitive bids accepted was 100.25 pounds, with a yield of 6.94 percent. Non-competitive bids were accepted at this price.
